one_liner: MongoDB Atlas Administration API is a broad REST API with free self-serve service accounts (OAuth2 client credentials) or digest API keys, plus an official MCP server.
auth_notes: Self-serve: service accounts (OAuth2 client-credentials) and legacy API keys using HTTP Digest (a variant of Basic-like key auth; labelled API_KEY and BASIC here). Delegated user OAuth 2.1 (Atlas App Connections) is invite-only, so multi-user access is per-customer service account or API key setup.
access_notes: Free Atlas account and free M0 cluster; service accounts/API keys created by an Organization Owner. Delegated OAuth is invite-only via partner onboarding.
blocker_notes: Per-customer setup: users must create a service account or API key as Organization Owner (with IP access list possibly). Delegated OAuth for multi-user is invite-only. The Admin API does not access cluster data.

evidence.quote: We recommend you use service accounts instead of API keys to authenticate to the Atlas Administration API. API keys are a legacy authentication method.
The API accepts 2 different authentication methods: Digest auth (http) Service accounts (oauth2)
MongoDB Atlas OAuth is currently **invite-only**. Client credentials are **not self-provisioned** — MongoDB provisions them manually on your behalf.
To create a service account or API keys for an organization, you must have Organization Owner access to that organization.
The Atlas Administration API doesn't provide access to the data stored in your clusters.
connects to the MongoDB-hosted Atlas MCP server over OAuth. This does not require you to run anything locally, and is the recommended way to connect to MongoDB Atlas
